description.value: The study examined whether anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, paired with speech-language therapy, altered resting-state functional connectivity and whether connectivity changes were associated with improvements in written naming in people with primary progressive aphasia.

design.value: Participants were drawn from a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover clinical trial, but the present analysis used only the first stimulation phase in a between-subject design comparing participants initially assigned to tDCS versus sham, with both groups receiving speech-language therapy.

description.value: Used to rate severity in primary progressive aphasia; language severity was based on the language subset and total severity referred to the sum of boxes, including language and behavior.

Percentage of letters corresponding to sounds making up words, scored with a rule-based system in which letters received points for correctness and points were subtracted for deletions, additions, substitutions, transpositions, or movements.
Participants reported their general pain levels one or two times during each stimulation session.
Letter fluency, sum of categories and words generated in 1 min.
Object naming, 30 total.
Action naming, 35 total.

source_definition.value: S = 1 for tDCS, S = 0 for sham.
Change in the Fisher z-transformed interregional correlation between before and after intervention.
Change in percentage of correct letters from before to after treatment for trained words.

description.value: Participants initially assigned to anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, simultaneous with speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: All had a history of at least two years of progressive language deficits; mean years post onset was 5.5 (3.5), and mean language severity was 1.9 (0.9) on the FTD-CDR.

description.value: Participants initially assigned to a sham procedure paired with speech-language therapy.

clinical_characteristics.value: All had a history of at least two years of progressive language deficits; mean years post onset was 4.3 (2.4), and mean language severity was 1.8 (0.7) on the FTD-CDR.

task_description.value: Each condition consisted of 15 sessions of daily therapy. The language therapy involved oral and written picture naming/spelling therapy using a spell-study-spell procedure. Participants practiced 10–30 words and were evaluated on matched untrained words.

design_type.value: between-subject first-phase comparison within a larger double-blinded, within-subject crossover design

instructions.value: Participants were shown a picture, asked to orally name the object, and then write it down; semantic cues, the correct word, corrective feedback, and spelling rehearsal were provided as needed.

stimuli.value: Pictures of trained words and matched untrained words.

task_performance_measures.value: letter accuracy, percentage of correct letters in trained words

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Resting-state fMRI data were acquired before, after, and two months post-intervention. Data were collected for approximately 9 min with 210 time-point acquisitions.

instrument.value: 3 T Philips Achieva MRI scanner equipped with a 32-channel head coil

description.value: Axial structural scans with a scan time of 6 min and 150 slices, using a T1-weighted MPRAGE sequence with 3D inversion recovery and magnetization-prepared rapid gradient.

Structural scans were parcellated into 283 structures using MRICloud. Resting-state fMRI was processed with coregistration, motion and slice timing correction, physiological nuisance correction using CompCor, and motion and intensity TR outlier rejection using ART. ROI time courses were extracted and correlations were Fisher z-transformed.

steps.value: MPRAGE segmentation and atlas-based parcellation into 283 structures using multi-atlas fusion label algorithm and large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping
Co-registration of structural labels to resting-state fMRI space
Motion correction and slice timing correction
Outlier TR rejection using ART, with thresholds of 2 standard deviations for motion and 4 standard deviations for intensity
Regression of the movement matrix and physiological nuisance matrix from the remaining TRs
Extraction of time courses from 19 cortical and deep gray matter ROIs and calculation of Pearson correlations followed by Fisher z transformation
ROI volume normalization by total intracerebral volume

model_settings.value: Difference in absolute change in percentage correct from before and after treatment was compared between tDCS and sham groups; one-sample t-tests assessed within-group changes.

For each ROI pair, baseline Fisher z-transformed correlation, age, sex, years post-onset, PPA variant, language severity, total FTD-CDR severity, and baseline left IFG volume were considered as covariates. Forward model selection used Akaike information criterion separately for tDCS and sham groups; standard sandwich estimation adjusted standard errors for small sample size; Wald statistics were used for hypothesis testing and Holm correction controlled the FWER.

estimator.value: standard sandwich estimator approach with asymptotic two-sided Wald tests

model_settings.value: For each ROI pair with an unadjusted treatment-effect P-value < .05, change in letter accuracy was regressed against change in functional connectivity correlation; t-tests were performed on model coefficients.

description.value: Anodal tDCS over the left inferior frontal gyrus, delivered simultaneously with the start of language therapy at 2 mA for a maximum of 20 min.
Sham procedure paired with speech-language therapy; current was ramped up at onset and ramped down to 0 mA after 30 s.
Words practiced at each session of either tDCS or sham stimulation.
Matched words not practiced but tested before treatment and at follow-up points.
